name: Methi Muthiya
subtitle: steamed fenugreek dumplings squeezed by hand, then tossed in a sesame tempering

ingredients.note: for a coarser, more traditional crumb

prepNotes: Salt the chopped methi and rest it 10 minutes, then squeeze hard. The water it gives up is usually enough to bind the dough with no extra liquid.
Oil the steamer plate well and oil your palms before shaping, or the dough sticks to everything.
Muthiya must cool completely before slicing, so build in 20 minutes of waiting before the tempering stage.

steps.text: Mix the flours, sesame, ajwain, ground spices, sugar, salt, ginger, chilli and lemon juice in a bowl.
Add the squeezed methi and 2 tbsp of the oil and work it into a stiff dough, using the methi water only if needed.
steps.tip: Keep it firm. Slack dough collapses in the steamer.

steps.text: Work in the baking soda, then divide the dough into four and roll each into a log about 4cm thick, squeezing it in your fist so it keeps the finger marks that give muthiya its name.
Steam the logs 20 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean and the surface is dry.
Cool completely, at least 20 minutes, then cut into 2cm slices.
steps.tip: Slicing warm muthiya tears it into crumbs.

steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in a kadhai, pop the mustard seeds, and add the curry leaves and asafoetida.
Add the slices and pan-fry 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until the cut faces are golden and crisp.
steps.tip: Turn rarely, not constantly — each face needs contact time to colour.

steps.text: Scatter the coconut and coriander over and serve hot with tea or masala chai.

storage: Steamed logs keep 4 days refrigerated. Slice and fry to order; fried muthiya keeps 2 days and crisps up again in a hot dry pan.
